findings.claim: GPU energy per batch of a float32 build of the common Gaussian VI workload

hypothesis: Lower precision buys nothing once roundoff dominates: float32 RK4 matches float64 until truncation error reaches float32 roundoff, and the float32 Gaussian VI iteration meets the workload's declared KL target as early as float64 but stalls at a roundoff floor below it; the counted operations per step or iteration are precision-independent, so any energy difference comes from how the hardware executes them, which only a capture can show.
input_data: 6 equatorial sphere geodesics, L = 3.0, N in [16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048]
the common Gaussian VI workload (examples/energy-accuracy/problem.json), float64 and float32, iterations 0..256; K = 38 and 4096 replicas per batch in a capture
optional operator capture bound as rapl-log (--capture rapl-log=PATH or CIW_LAB_RAPL_LOG)
mathematical_model: RK4: global error ~ C h^4 + c N u with u = 2^-24 (float32) or 2^-53 (float64); cost ~ 4 N right-hand-side evaluations. Gaussian VI: a contraction toward the posterior, so KL decays geometrically until the iterate's rounding (relative u) leaves KL ~ u^2 above zero; cost replicas x (24 K + 7) operations per batch in either precision.
numerical_result: float64 RK4 order 3.963; float32 crossover minimum 5.83e-07 at N = 64, plateau median 2.46e-06 for N >= 128; smallest grid N per target {'0.0001': {'float32': 16, 'float64': 16}, '1e-05': {'float32': 32, 'float64': 32}, '1e-07': {'float32': None, 'float64': 128}, '1e-10': {'float32': None, 'float64': 512}, '1e-11': {'float32': None, 'float64': 1024}}; Gaussian VI first iteration meeting 1e-08 nats: {'float64': 38, 'float32': 38}; float32 KL floor 2.43e-14 at iteration 66; float64 reaches 1e-14 at iteration 69; energy: not measured (no accepted RAPL capture).
observation_model: RK4 endpoints computed entirely in the declared dtype, mapped to R^3 and compared in float64 with the exact great circle; Gaussian VI outputs computed entirely in the declared dtype and scored in float64 by KL to the exact posterior (ciw.free_energy_math); a bound capture's float64 and float32 brackets give package energy per batch.

physical_validation_status.statement: Physical validation requires acquired hardware evidence; none was acquired for this task.

title: Compare precision versus energy cost.
uncertainty: float32 RK4 errors depend on the platform's float32 sin/cos and vary by tens of percent; the Gaussian VI iteration uses no library function, so its float32 and float64 values are exact IEEE results, scored against a binary64 reference whose own rounding shows below about 1e-30 nats; a RAPL energy would carry model error and background load.
unresolved_assumptions: Operation counts do not capture memory traffic, vector width, transcendental cost or GPU float32 throughput; only a capture relates precision to energy
The NumPy reference runs each precision vectorized across replicas; CPU energy per batch reflects that implementation, not the GPU kernel

Both precision brackets share one boundary (telemetry.NUMPY_BOUNDARY): the prepared inputs are computed once before bracketing and excluded; each batch includes the rounding of the 15 inputs to its precision and their broadcast to the replica columns

implementation missing: no float32 implementation of the gaussian_vi PTX kernel exists (ciw.energy_cuda is binary64 only, and `ciw energy record` captures only it), so a float32 GPU workload cannot run on any host

Deferred research question: extend the common workload's GPU path beyond the binary64 gaussian_vi PTX kernel of ciw.energy_cuda: a float32 rendering of the same kernel, and a device-wide reduction of its per-replica outputs (a fixed tree over the stored order per T148's REDUCTION_POLICY, plus one atomicAdd variant), each compared with the NumPy reference by compare_outputs on the RTX 2080 host and captured with `ciw energy record` for energy; until then those claims stay not_established on every host
